doc.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023

title: Getting on camera at SNL: Howard Shore, 'The Magic Show' and the Don Kirshner sketch
summary: Shaffer recounts coming to New York for 'The Magic Show', joining SNL, a Hollywood pilot, and his first on-air bit as Don Kirshner.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I should fast forward a little bit. When you got into the SNL band and were there for a while, did the writers start to recognize that you would be a useful character in skits? Like the Star Wars thing on the train? How did that occur?

Well I was sort of sizing things up and saying to myself how can I get on camera. You know it totally was. Whether it was subconscious or whether I knew what I was doing or not, that’s just the kind of kid I was, kind of repressed I guess on the outside but dying to break out. And well a couple of crazy things happened. The first year, no even before you know my first job in town was a Broadway show, “The Magic Show.” Steven Schwartz, the Broadway composer, brought me in to town. Because I had played “Godspell” for him up in Toronto and now here I am, he moved me to New York and got me my first visa etcetera. And while that was happening one of these “Godspell” types, actor types got me an audition and I ended up going to Hollywood and making a TV pilot, which was unsuccessful at the time, and then SNL started. That was because where there was Canadians involved I knew Howard Shore, the bandleader from Toronto. After “Godspell” I met him on the next show I did — I was kind of theatrical up there, dealing with music, written music that I never thought I would but you know learning how to negotiate a chart, even if I couldn’t make all the notes within the bar. I certainly knew the sign goes back to here and you know things that are still important. And whatever the question was it’s long gone.
Well you found yourself on camera in part of —

Oh yeah how’d I get on camera. Well yeah so I left, they took that pilot off the shelf and I ended up leaving SNL in the second season and going to Hollywood and making a show that played called “Year at the Top” it didn’t get picked up, came back got my old job back. But now I had some ammunition. I had seen this guy Don Kirchner. He had a show at the time, “Don Kirchner’s Rock Concert.” He emceed it in a really funny deadpan way. I am now back at SNL kind of participating in writing sessions. And Brian Doyle Murray, Billy’s brother, had this idea — Brian Doyle Murray, a writer and a good friend of mine because he had been in Toronto, another whole story. But he said, “I’ve got this idea, Garret Morris, the only black guy on the cast at that time, what if he’s in drag as Tina Turner and he sings “Proud Mary” which he did a bang-up job of in high heels. But we’ve got to explain it’s like instead of he’s Tina Turner but instead of Ike it’s Mr. Mike, one of our running characters. It’s Mr. Mike and Tina Turner. How can we set this up and so the audience understands it before Garret comes out in those heels? And I just said, “Well I could do the guy Don Kirchner who has that show. I happened to have worked
with him, you know, and I can do an impression of him.” And he said, “Great.” And that’s how I sneaked on the air for the first time.
